Angular has grown into one of the most mature frameworks for building enterprise-grade web applications. Every major release has introduced improvements that simplify development, improve performance, and reduce boilerplate. Features like standalone components, Signals, built-in control flow, deferred loading, and server-side rendering have made Angular more capable than ever.
Yet writing Angular applications today isn’t without challenges.
As projects become larger, developers often struggle with application architecture, state management, performance, testing, dependency updates, and maintaining clean code. The framework itself is powerful, but choosing the right approach is becoming increasingly important.
